title: Inconsistent API reference format requirements across commands
description: The platform accepts vendor/name format in some contexts (e.g., `jentic apis`) but requires vendor/name/version in others (e.g., `jentic inspect`). This creates confusion about which format is correct and forces users to trial-and-error.
reproduction_steps: Run `jentic apis` and find an API like 'jentic-test/test-api'
Attempt to inspect it with `jentic inspect jentic-test/test-api`
expected_behavior: API references should accept a consistent format across all commands, or the CLI should auto-resolve the version if only one exists.
actual_behavior: Some commands accept vendor/name while others require vendor/name/version, forcing users to discover the correct format through trial-and-error.
evidence: error: invalid API reference "jentic-test/test-api"; expected vendor/name/version
API reference format inconsistency: agent encountered errors requiring version suffix (vendor/name/version) in some contexts but not others

title: CLI header format validation rejects standard colon-separated syntax
description: The `--header` flag rejects the standard HTTP header format (key: value) and requires key=value format instead. This is non-standard and conflicts with common CLI conventions.
reproduction_steps: Attempt to add a header with `--header X-API-Key: test-key`
expected_behavior: The CLI should accept standard HTTP header format (key: value) or at minimum provide a clear error message explaining the required format upfront.
actual_behavior: The CLI rejects colon-separated headers with a cryptic error message, requiring users to use key=value format instead.
evidence: error: invalid --header value "X-API-Key: test-key"; expected key=value

title: Toolkit request action values not discoverable from help text
description: The platform rejects `--action create` with an error stating valid values are 'bind' or 'grant', but the help text or error message does not explain when to use each action or provide examples.
reproduction_steps: Discover correct values only through error message
expected_behavior: Help text should document valid action values and their semantics, or the error message should include guidance on which action to use.
actual_behavior: The error message lists valid values but provides no context on when to use 'bind' vs 'grant'.
evidence: Toolkit access request flow required multiple command attempts; agent encountered errors with invalid action values ('create' vs 'bind'/'grant')
